1.  The plaintiff filed the present suit for recovery of Rs 2,24,600/- with interest @ 18% per annum.

2. Brief facts as alleged in the plaint and documents filed by the plaintiff are that plaintiff is the exclusive owner in possession of property no. D-1/97, Sector- 16, Rohini, Delhi admeasuring 48 sq meters (hereinafter referred to as 'suit property') and the said property is his self acquired property.

It is averred that AJAY by AJAY SINGH SINGH PARIHAR Date: 2025.05.09 PARIHAR 15:11:42 +0530 defendants are the youngest daughter in law and son of plaintiff who were earlier living with plaintiff in the suit property but since they used to do quarrels with family and his family members

,
there are multiple litigations pending amongst them.
It is averred that the conduct of defendants had made the life of plaintiff a living hell.

It is averred that on 27.06.2012, the defendants left the suit property and started living separately at G-7/39, Sector-15, Rohini, however, while leaving the suit property, they left their almirah, sofa and double bed in the suit property and undertook to remove their articles within 15 days.
It is averred that the defendants did not come back to remove their belongings.
It is averred that later on, defendant no. 1 lodged a false case FIR No. 123/2023 PS K N Katju Marg u/s 498A/376/ 354/313/511/506/34 IPC against the plaintiff and his family members.

It is averred that when defendants failed to remove their belongings from the suit property and registered a false FIR against the planitiff, the plaintiff filed a suit for permanent and mandatory injunction vide CS No. 107/2013 against the defendants in which defendants were first proceeded exparte and the order of exparte was set aside and consequently, a decree u/o XII rule 6 CPC was passed vide order dated 24.11.2014 and the defendants were directed to remove the articles Kharati Ram Ranga vs Manju Bala Mehra Anr on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135312048/
1 from the suit property.

3. It is averred that despite undertaking, defendants failed to remove their articles and therefore,
plaintiff filed execution petition wherein with the help of bailiff, the plaintiff took the possession of suit property but none of the defendants came forward to take their articles back.

It is averred that other son of plaintiff got superdari of all the articles, which were lying in the suit property and thereafter all the articles were removed from suit property and placed in rented premises of Sh.
Bishan Dayal Sharma who charged rent of premises @ 5,000/- per month from 08.06.2016 to 06.10.2016 totaling to Rs 20,000/-.
It is averred that plaintiff thereafter moved application for disposing off all the articles of defendant but on 06.10.2016 defendants received their articles from the plaintiff.

Plaintiff was shocked to see the condition of suit property as it AJAY by AJAY SINGH SINGH PARIHAR Date: 2025.05.09 PARIHAR 15:11:48 +0530 became worst/ damaged due to locked position due to illegal possession of defendants.
4. The suit property was got inspected by Architect who gave an estimate of Rs 24,600/- to get the suit property repaired.
It is averred that due to illegal possession of defendants, plaintiff has been burdened with loss of Rs 44,600/-.

It is averred that sicne the defendants illegally kept occupying the suit property, therefore, both the defendants are jointly and severally liable to pay damages to the tune of Rs 10,000/- per month w.e.f. 24.11.2014 and 08.06.2016 (date on which locks were broken by bailiff) amounting to Rs 1,80,000/-.
Aggrieved, the plaintiff has filed the present suit for recovery of damages and mesne profits.

5. Upon service of summons, defendants appeared in the Court, however, the defendant failed to file W.S and their opportunity to file W/S was closed and they were they were proceeded exparte on 15.07.2016.
6.

Thereafter, defendants started appearing in the matter and filed written statement thereby stating that the suit property was purchased from the funds of ancestral property and thus, defendant no. 2 has share in it.
It is averred that plaintiff has not filed any ownership document.
It is averred that since the suit property is not his self acquired, plaintiff has not filed any registered sale deed etc.

It is averred that defendants were regularly paying rent to plaintiff's mother and had paid Rs 1,50,000/-
to plaintiff through cheque before leaving the property on 27.06.2012.

It is stated that when the bailiff opened the lock of the property, some articles of defendants were missing and therefore,
defendants did not take rest of the articles and filed FIR No. 1176/2015 on 06.11.2015 u/s 380 IPC against the plaintiff.
It is averred that present suit is undervalued.
It is also averred that no damages were assessed while passing of decree in earlier suit, hence present suit is not maintainable.
It is also averred that inspection report is false as the suit property is two storey whereas the inspection report mentions it as four storey building.

15. Issue no.1 - Whether the plaintiff is entitled for recovery of amount of Rs 2,24,600/- as damages,
as prayed for?
The defendants have not cross examined the plaintiff and other two witnesses, hence their testimony remained unrebutted and unchallenged.
17. It is averred by defendants that suit property is ancestral property and that plaintiff has not filed any document of ownership.

The plaintiff has averred in plaint that an earlier civil suit bearing no.
107/13 titled as Sh. Kharati Ram Ranga vs Smt. Manju Bala Mehra and Sh. Sanjay Kumar Ranga,
was filed by present plaintiff against present defendants for permanent and mandatory injunction wherein the defendant admitted the claim of plaintiff and a decree was passed u/o 12 rule 6 of CPC.

sentences.text:
The defendants in response to the averment made in plaint regarding this earlier suit and decree,
have averred in WS that civil suit filed by plaintiff is matter of record and same is denied for want of knowledge, therefore, need no reply.
The response of defendants is evasive as clearly the earlier judgment and decree were passed against defendants which has given cause of action of the present case.
In application u/o 14 rule 5 CPC, defendants have admitted that plaintiff had field previous suit for permanent and mandatory injunction.
It is matter of record that earlier suit was filed for present suit property, which was decreed on the admissions of defendants.

18. Plaintiff has filed copy of a page of earlier plaint and copy of order and decree dated 24.11.2024 in civil suit bearing no. 107/13 titled as Sh. Kharati Ram Ranga vs Smt. Manju Bala Mehra and Sh.
Sanjay Kumar Ranga, wherein the defendants herein made a statement that they shall not enter into the suit property (property no. D-197, Sector 16, Rohini) and shall not interfere in the peaceful enjoyment, accommodation and possession of the suit property of the AJAY by AJAY SINGH SINGH PARIHAR

sentences.text: Date: 2025.05.09 PARIHAR 15:12:08 +0530 plaintiff.
The copy of plaint shows the averment of plaintiff in earlier suit was that he is the exclusive owner of suit property.
The decree was passed u/o 12 rule 6 CPC on the admission of defendants.

As per decree dated 24.11.2014, the defendants were are restrained by way of permanent injunction from entering forcibly into the suit property and also directed to take possession of their Almirah, sofa set, double bed and other articles lying in the suit property by way of mandatory injunction.
Since the earlier suit was decreed on the basis of admission, it is not open for defendants to reagitate the fact of ownership due to issue estoppel.
Even otherwise plaintiff has not been cross examined on this aspect hence this averment reminded bald statement without any substance.
19. It is also averred that defendants were regularly paying rent to plaintiff's mother and had paid Rs 1,50,000/- to plaintiff through cheque before leaving the property on 27.06.2012.

The defendants have not placed on record any documentary proof of payment and even otherwise this payment has been made for rent till 27.06.2012 whereas in the present case plaintiff is seeking rent for four months from 08.06.2016 till 06.10.2016, damages and illegal occupation charges from 24.11.2014 till 08.06.2016.
Even if the defendants have paid this amount then also this payment is wholly irrelevant for the determination of present issue.

The plaintiff has submitted that when the possession of suit property was handed over by the help of bailiff on 08.06.2016, the suit property was found to be having articles of defendants.

It is submitted that all the articles were removed from suit property and placed in rented premises of Sh.
Bishan Dayal Sharma who charged rent of premises @ 5,000/- per month from 08.06.2016 to 06.10.2016 totaling to Rs 20,000/-.
PW 2 Sh. Bishan Dayal Sharma proved rent receipt Ex PW1/1 (Colly) which have been issued to plaintiff.
Hence this court has not reason to disbelieve the payment of rent by the plaintiff.
For proving the damages, the plaintiff examined PW3 Sh. Laxman Singh, draftsman/civil engineer who proved his report Ex. PW1/2.
This report AJAY by AJAY SINGH SINGH PARIHAR Date: 2025.05.09 PARIHAR 15:12:13 +0530 remained unrebutted.
It is averred in the WS that this report is false as the suit property is two storey whereas report states that suit property is four storey building.

The defendants have neither cross examined PW3 nor placed on record any evidence to show that suit property is four storey building, hence this averment of defendants remained bald statement without any substance.

21. The plaintiff has also claimed illegal occupation charges from 24.11.2014 till 08.06.2016 @
10,000/- per month.
The plaintiff has proved that decree of permanent and mandatory injunction was passed on 24.11.2014 and the possession of suit property was handed over on 08.06.2016.

The defendants were directed to remove their articles from the suit property, however defendants did not remove the articles and plaintiff had to keep articles in a tenanted premises for which he paid rent.
In paragraph 7 of WS, defendants have admitted that they did not remove the articles from the suit property on the ground that some articles were missing.
It is also averred that defendants lodged FIR for the same.

The admission by defendant in WS leaves no doubt that the articles were lying in suit premises, the fact of FIR and missing articles are wholly irrelevant for determination of present issue as defendants were clearly directed by way of mandatory injunction to remove their articles from suit property.
The plaintiff has not placed on record any documentary proof of rate of rent for the relevant time in the locality to show that rate of rent was 10,000/- per month.

It is an admitted fact that plaintiff paid a rent of 5000/- per month for the period of 08.06.2016 to 06.10.2016, hence in absence of any other documentary proof it is safe to consider this rate of rent as rent for illegal occupation charges.
Hence 5000/- will be taken as rate of rent for illegal occupation charges per month from 24.11.2014 till 08.06.2016.
22. In view of the above discussion, the plaintiff has discharged the burden lying on him, hence issue no.1 is decide in favor of plaintiff.
23. Issue no. 2 - Whether the present suit is barred by law in light of provisions of Order 2 rule 2 CPC r.w.s. 11 CPC?
(OPD) AJAY by AJAY SINGH SINGH PARIHAR

The burden for proving second issue is on defendants, however the defendants neither cross examined the plaintiff and other witnesses nor brought any evidence to discharge the burden qua present issue.
Hence this issue is decided against the defendants and in favor of plaintiff.

25. Costs of the suit are awarded in favour of the plaintiff.
